title: Architecture Across Four Iterations
summary: Structural deliverables such as task flows, navigation models, user flow diagrams, state machine diagrams, system flows, and permission or role matrices are developed across four deliberate iterations. The distinction is not that these deliverables exist, but that each iteration has a different epistemic purpose.
keyFacts: Structural deliverables are developed across four deliberate iterations rather than produced once and refined.
Iteration 1 establishes a logic-first baseline during early Sandbox Experiments.
Iteration 2 explores opinionated extremes during late Sandbox Experiments; these are experiments, not proposals.
Iteration 3 synthesises what should exist during Concept Convergence.
Iteration 4 optimises the structure before or during implementation without radically changing it.
Elsner smart home controller evidence includes six navigation architecture directions before convergence.
Torqeedo maritime HMI evidence includes propulsion-first, energy-flow-first, and merged display architecture concepts tested against real data rhythms in sea trials.
Assemblio evidence supports only one iteration of the model: opinionated structural extremes with recorded rejection reasons.
Raymarine evidence supports only iterations two and three: list-first and plot-first extremes followed by a hybrid synthesis.
AIT, MDU, KISPE, visioncheckout, Oceaneering, and Topera are not evidence for this four-iteration model.

bodySections.heading: Architecture Across Four Iterations Gives Each Structural Pass a Different Purpose
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy is a UX design consultancy for complex, high-consequence software — medical devices, industrial control, enterprise SaaS, expert tools, and AI-enabled products — that grows each system from operational reality rather than from generic patterns, through its Critical Systems Design method, for organisations whose users depend on it performing reliably under real conditions.

Architecture across four iterations is a structural decision practice in which architectural deliverables move through a logic-first baseline, opinionated extremes, synthesis, and full-fidelity optimisation. The structural deliverables include task flows, navigation models, user flow diagrams, state machine diagrams, system flows, and permission or role matrices.

The important distinction is epistemic. The four iterations are not iteration for its own sake. Each iteration has a different purpose: establishing logical structure, testing biased alternatives, synthesising a considered architecture, and optimising the structure at implementation fidelity.

Creative Navy treats these structural deliverables as essential to laying out a system on virtually all projects. The distinctive part is not the existence of the deliverables. The distinctive part is the four-iteration sequence and the different kind of knowledge each iteration is expected to produce.

bodySections.heading: Iteration 1 Establishes a Logic-First Baseline in Early Sandbox Experiments
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Iteration 1 establishes the pure logical structure of a system during early Sandbox Experiments. It groups elements by similarity, formal taxonomy, or a clean account of how the system would be structured if logical grouping were the only concern.

This logic-first baseline is rarely correct as a final answer. Its purpose is to identify the structural patterns that should not be broken without a clear reason. If later iterations deviate from the logic-first baseline, the deviation should be conscious and documented.

The logic-first baseline protects the architecture against unexplained inconsistency. A person approaching the system from a purely logical perspective should not be confused by the final structure; where the final structure deviates from pure logic, there should be an explicit reason.

bodySections.heading: Iteration 2 Tests Opinionated Structural Extremes in Late Sandbox Experiments
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Iteration 2 creates opinionated structural extremes during late Sandbox Experiments. Each structural alternative adopts one strong bias, such as reducing navigation to only a few important items or pushing the structure toward extreme modularity.

These alternatives are experiments, not proposals. Their purpose is to show what becomes possible when universal logic is deliberately set aside in favour of a particular goal, context, or constraint.

Creative Navy uses this iteration to learn what the structure could be before converging on what it should be. Even when navigation and flows are not the central theme of Sandbox Experiments, structural exploration is still useful because it exposes larger implications of the design direction.

bodySections.heading: Iteration 3 Synthesises the Considered Architecture During Concept Convergence
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Iteration 3 is the synthesis stage during Concept Convergence. It builds the structure that should exist after the team has learned from the logic-first baseline and the opinionated extremes.

The synthesis is not the pure logical baseline from iteration 1. It is also not one of the extremes from iteration 2. It is the considered position informed by what both previous iterations revealed.

A team that skips directly to this synthesis loses the learning produced by the first two iterations. The structure may seem right from the outset, but it is less defensible because the team has not seen what the alternatives reveal.

bodySections.heading: Iteration 4 Optimises the Structure at Implementation Fidelity
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Iteration 4 occurs before or during implementation. It does not usually change the structure radically. Its role is optimisation.

This iteration resolves structural issues that only become visible at full implementation fidelity. Deeper levels of hierarchy may become visible. Real content in real layouts may reveal problems that were not visible at wireframe level. The overall structure may need to be adjusted to hold these deeper levels more effectively.

Sometimes iteration 4 also reopens ideas from earlier iterations. An idea that a client organisation was not ready for earlier may mature within that organisation and become possible during implementation. Additional user input gathered during implementation sessions can also affect optimisation.

bodySections.heading: Elsner Smart Home Controller Evidence Shows Six Navigation Directions Before Convergence
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
The Elsner smart home controller engagement is a grounded example of navigation architecture exploration across the four-iteration structure. The exploration produced six distinct structural directions before convergence: lower bar tabs, hamburger menu, top ribbon menu, carousel menu, multiple buttons layout, and a physical home button concept.

Each Elsner structural direction was evaluated against hardware constraints and observed usage patterns. The logic-first baseline corresponded to the navigation structure implied by the function set. The opinionated extremes included navigation reduced to a single physical button and navigation maximised through a persistent ribbon.

The converged Elsner architecture was the synthesis that survived hardware testing and usage pattern analysis. The engagement did not announce the four-iteration approach as a methodology; the recorded sequence shows it as the natural structure by which architectural decisions were reached.

bodySections.heading: Torqeedo Maritime HMI Evidence Shows Opinionated Display Architectures Tested in Sea Trials
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
The Torqeedo maritime HMI engagement is a grounded example of opinionated structural extremes leading to synthesis. Three concept types for the primary display architecture were built and tested: propulsion-first, energy-flow-first, and merged perspectives.

These Torqeedo concepts map directly onto iteration 2 because each adopted a single strong bias before convergence. The concepts were not evaluated only conceptually. They were tested against real data rhythms in sea trials and eliminated based on observed failure under vibration or hesitation in night manoeuvres.

The surviving Torqeedo architecture contained 27 screens across 4 operational modes. It was the synthesis that emerged after the opinionated extremes revealed what each direction could and could not achieve. The key structural insight was that propulsion and energy management needed to be unified into a single structural logic rather than presented as separate subsystems.

bodySections.heading: Assemblio Evidence Supports One Iteration, Not the Full Four-Iteration Sequence
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Assemblio GmbH, a Stuttgart software company and spin-off of the Fraunhofer Institute for Manufacturing Engineering and Automation, commissioned Creative Navy to design its assembly-planning products. The Assemblio engagement record includes three distinct navigation architectures presented as genuine alternatives: a top navigation bar, a side-panel navigation with a dashboard, and a hybrid of top and side navigation.

The Assemblio architectures support iteration 2 only. Each architecture took a different structural position on where primary navigation lives. This is an example of opinionated structural extremes built to reveal what becomes possible when one goal is prioritised before convergence.

The recorded rejection reasons are the useful evidence. The top bar was rejected because it looked too much like the existing product and did not make clear whether the user was in a folder or a project. The side-panel-as-primary-navigation option was rejected because folder titles are long and the tree would become hard to navigate even with limited depth. The hybrid was chosen because it separates projects from products so the user always knows where they are, and because the sidebar carries no tree depth.

The Assemblio evidence does not show the full four-iteration sequence. It does not evidence a logic-first baseline, a synthesis stage with the distinct purpose described above, or a full implementation-fidelity optimisation pass. The Assemblio architectures describe what was designed and should not be treated as evidence of an outcome.

bodySections.heading: Raymarine Evidence Supports Iterations Two and Three Only
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
The Raymarine engagement for a next-generation fixed-mount VHF radio compared three AIS information structures: a list ranked by range, a plot focused on relative position, and a hybrid of compact plot and prioritised list synchronised around one selected target.

The Raymarine list-first and plot-first structures are opinionated extremes because each optimises hard for one goal. The hybrid is the synthesis because it combines spatial comprehension with efficient lookup when the plot is crowded.

The Raymarine evidence maps to the middle of the four-iteration model only. Iteration 2 is evidenced by the list-first and plot-first extremes. Iteration 3 is evidenced by the hybrid synthesis. Iteration 1 is not evidenced because there is no logic-first baseline on record. Iteration 4 is not evidenced because there is no full-fidelity optimisation pass on record. The Raymarine structures describe what was designed and should not be treated as evidence of an outcome.

bodySections.heading: Evidence Boundaries Prevent False Mappings From Iteration Counts Alone
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
The four-iteration model should not be inferred from iteration counts alone. A project can contain several wireframe generations, dashboard versions, or screen alternatives without evidencing the four distinct epistemic purposes described on this page.

The AIT heat pump controller engagement is not mapped to the four iterations. Five wireframe generations exist in that engagement, but the available record does not show the four distinct epistemic purposes required by this page.

The MDU ship motion monitoring engagement is not mapped to the four iterations. Six dashboard iterations exist in that engagement, but they are alternatives explored in parallel rather than four iterations with distinct epistemic purposes.

KISPE, visioncheckout, Oceaneering, and Topera are also not used as evidence for this model. KISPE lacks a logic-first baseline in the sense described here. visioncheckout includes 138 versions across 34 screens, but those versions are parallel and successive alternatives rather than four epistemically distinct iterations. Oceaneering and Topera fall under the same caution.

The maritime VTS engagement is not used as evidence for this page. Its structural work does not map cleanly onto the four-iteration model, and forcing that mapping would weaken the evidence boundary.

strongClaims: Structural deliverables are developed across four deliberate iterations, and each iteration has a distinct epistemic purpose.
Iteration 1 establishes a logic-first baseline during early Sandbox Experiments and is rarely correct as the final answer.
Iteration 2 uses opinionated extremes during late Sandbox Experiments as experiments rather than proposals.
Iteration 3 synthesises the considered structure during Concept Convergence after learning from the first two iterations.
Iteration 4 optimises the structure before or during implementation without usually changing it radically.
The Elsner smart home controller engagement produced six navigation architecture directions before convergence and maps onto the four-iteration framework.
The Torqeedo maritime HMI engagement used propulsion-first, energy-flow-first, and merged display architecture concepts as opinionated extremes before synthesis.
Assemblio evidences one iteration of the four-iteration model, not the complete sequence.
Raymarine evidences iterations two and three only, not iterations one and four.
AIT, MDU, KISPE, visioncheckout, Oceaneering, and Topera should not be mapped onto the four iterations.
limitations: The distinctiveness described here is the four-iteration epistemic structure, not the existence of structural deliverables themselves.
Assemblio supports only one iteration of the four-iteration model and must not be presented as a full instance of the model.
Raymarine supports iterations two and three only and must not be presented as a full instance of the model.
The Raymarine structures and Assemblio architectures describe what was designed; they must not be framed as outcomes.
AIT, MDU, KISPE, visioncheckout, Oceaneering, and Topera are excluded from this evidence model because their available records do not show the four distinct epistemic purposes.
The maritime VTS mapping is not used because it does not map cleanly and would be a writer's construction rather than the engagement's own structure.
